Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 59, "heading": "CHAPTER 57. THE EMIGRANTS", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u059-b0030", "target": "— Эмма, — отвечал он, — этот взгляд на вопрос в такой миг неотразим. Я не могу, даже теперь, определённо обещать, что брошусь на шею вашей семье; но член вашей семьи, который сейчас ожидает внизу, не найдёт в моём лице заморозителя своего доброго тепла.", "source_sha256": "0be10a1dc2f2129c691a0e63761d7d14332ff56a894eef5c7ee10d723edb05a4", "target_id": "ru-en85-u059-b0030", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "cac265781db5b31a2dbccd2d659949ca993d184d06f7a7feb8967ba5d1c9f266"}, {"source_id": "en85-u059-b0031", "target": "Мистер Микобер удалился и отсутствовал некоторое время; за это время миссис Микобер не была вполне свободна от опасения, что между ним и Членом могли возникнуть резкие слова. Наконец тот же мальчик появился снова и вручил мне записку, написанную карандашом и озаглавленную, на юридический манер, «Хип против Микобера». Из этого документа я узнал, что мистер Микобер, будучи вновь арестован, «находился в последнем пароксизме отчаяния и просил меня переслать ему с подателем сего его нож и пинтовую кружку, ибо они могут пригодиться ему в тюрьме в недолгий остаток его существования. Он просил также, как о последнем акте дружбы, чтобы я проводил его семью в Приходский Работный Дом и забыл, что такое Существо когда-либо жило на свете.", "source_sha256": "1e60b00b2c6570fbe7783ebbc90a0704df720a65f27544ecbe0303ed66d5448d", "target_id": "ru-en85-u059-b0031", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "49ab7a9cf6a75addeaa2b2197130446b87be18d1f1ea7ef8067fbb522465e54c"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 57, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u059-b0032", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Of course I answered this note by going down with the boy to pay the money, where I found Mr. Micawber sitting in a corner, looking darkly at the Sheriff‘s Officer who had effected the capture. On his release, he embraced me with the utmost fervour; and made an entry of the transaction in his pocket-book—being very particular, I recollect, about a halfpenny I inadvertently omitted from my statement of the total.", "sha256": "22e9909d5a41590217bbac94f687cc5c5ea9d37f9490ff0c24116c2576c21f37", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[33]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0033", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "This momentous pocket-book was a timely reminder to him of another transaction. On our return to the room upstairs (where he accounted for his absence by saying that it had been occasioned by circumstances over which he had no control), he took out of it a large sheet of paper, folded small, and quite covered with long sums, carefully worked. From the glimpse I had of them, I should say that I never saw such sums out of a school ciphering-book. These, it seemed, were calculations of compound interest on what he called ‘the principal amount of forty-one, ten, eleven and a half’, for various periods. After a careful consideration of these, and an elaborate estimate of his resources, he had come to the conclusion to select that sum which represented the amount with compound interest to two years, fifteen calendar months, and fourteen days, from that date. For this he had drawn a note-of-hand with great neatness, which he handed over to Traddles on the spot, a discharge of his debt in full (as between man and man), with many acknowledgements.", "sha256": "9227ab41528bb48ae2bd04e64f467bcb18d8b69fa5a425178eb3ac4bd05e39c1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[34]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0034", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I have still a presentiment,’ said Mrs. Micawber, pensively shaking her head, ‘that my family will appear on board, before we finally depart.’", "sha256": "22231f30d1fcd346a9e9e0e192d13484abfa8a185918d8b0149c46de860fe9f2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[35]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0035", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber evidently had his presentiment on the subject too, but he put it in his tin pot and swallowed it.", "sha256": "14b2fd81ec2c4ff8948218de115bc106f66220134510c993ed776f72628bf4bd", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[36]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0036", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘If you have any opportunity of sending letters home, on your passage, Mrs. Micawber,’ said my aunt, ‘you must let us hear from you, you know.’", "sha256": "de0f8ee429767fafa47f586f471d076699fc4f0a2985aae9545229f726cc758f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[37]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0037", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dear Miss Trotwood,’ she replied, ‘I shall only be too happy to think that anyone expects to hear from us. I shall not fail to correspond. Mr. Copperfield, I trust, as an old and familiar friend, will not object to receive occasional intelligence, himself, from one who knew him when the twins were yet unconscious?’", "sha256": "0598963c9f4fb7f0c4ff81fdc38e25ada359904c6f4ca48b65467e2e2555888d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[38]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0038", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I said that I should hope to hear, whenever she had an opportunity of writing.", "sha256": "ffe1176891c093a0b9319905ca69862e43eee7a11223d81341dd91483a6d6580", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[39]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0039", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Please Heaven, there will be many such opportunities,’ said Mr. Micawber. ‘The ocean, in these times, is a perfect fleet of ships; and we can hardly fail to encounter many, in running over. It is merely crossing,’ said Mr. Micawber, trifling with his eye-glass, ‘merely crossing. The distance is quite imaginary.’", "sha256": "8ca90ab5682278b408c24a0cc53a07ae1904180e9444731a09ecb3d365bb7949", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[40]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0040", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I think, now, how odd it was, but how wonderfully like Mr. Micawber, that, when he went from London to Canterbury, he should have talked as if he were going to the farthest limits of the earth; and, when he went from England to Australia, as if he were going for a little trip across the channel.", "sha256": "9556541b0d03e024949baa861a64eff93c2b1c7dce6c0d119cda893c5518ba37", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[41]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0041", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘On the voyage, I shall endeavour,’ said Mr. Micawber, ‘occasionally to spin them a yarn; and the melody of my son Wilkins will, I trust, be acceptable at the galley-fire. When Mrs. Micawber has her sea-legs on—an expression in which I hope there is no conventional impropriety—she will give them, I dare say, “Little Tafflin”. Porpoises and dolphins, I believe, will be frequently observed athwart our Bows; and, either on the starboard or the larboard quarter, objects of interest will be continually descried. In short,’ said Mr. Micawber, with the old genteel air, ‘the probability is, all will be found so exciting, alow and aloft, that when the lookout, stationed in the main-top, cries Land-oh! we shall be very considerably astonished!’", "sha256": "e9f217753fe0e854027be68e486977f1cdd07d440cacf120feb731d67d329248", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[42]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0042", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "With that he flourished off the contents of his little tin pot, as if he had made the voyage, and had passed a first-class examination before the highest naval authorities.", "sha256": "02c6acfa22ae516c6dfe38115eb6bb1aa085b456f2ad71866dd8e9a73a75841c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[43]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0043", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘What I chiefly hope, my dear Mr. Copperfield,’ said Mrs. Micawber, ‘is, that in some branches of our family we may live again in the old country. Do not frown, Micawber! I do not now refer to my own family, but to our children’s children. However vigorous the sapling,’ said Mrs. Micawber, shaking her head, ‘I cannot forget the parent-tree; and when our race attains to eminence and fortune, I own I should wish that fortune to flow into the coffers of Britannia.’", "sha256": "3c61d9db7a263fe8381c9dab86bd97dd6f282b611352b4a5e7331892f4d4284a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[44]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0044", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dear,’ said Mr. Micawber, ‘Britannia must take her chance. I am bound to say that she has never done much for me, and that I have no particular wish upon the subject.’", "sha256": "e65a27e39cbff4a8ce93ce4b66e2e55517684e553672527c4e7b8b876ccb6f3b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[45]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0045", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Micawber,’ returned Mrs. Micawber, ‘there, you are wrong. You are going out, Micawber, to this distant clime, to strengthen, not to weaken, the connexion between yourself and Albion.’", "sha256": "f500afecc9d1064fbe2b40004443d5bd66c50b6cf25fa7d9fc29108e425fcf41", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[46]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0046", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘The connexion in question, my love,’ rejoined Mr. Micawber, ‘has not laid me, I repeat, under that load of personal obligation, that I am at all sensitive as to the formation of another connexion.’", "sha256": "800e8a844bee909c1dd18b3bb305527521503b1101aafd1bdcc4102760fa82dc", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[47]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0047", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Micawber,’ returned Mrs. Micawber. ‘There, I again say, you are wrong. You do not know your power, Micawber. It is that which will strengthen, even in this step you are about to take, the connexion between yourself and Albion.’", "sha256": "7fcac4891565f0c2422716734d587811ca0d2acd71a5afb0138bab171ba3739d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[48]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0048", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber sat in his elbow-chair, with his eyebrows raised; half receiving and half repudiating Mrs. Micawber’s views as they were stated, but very sensible of their foresight.", "sha256": "7c285b7c85ae471de62154e76750d2629028154d6b5ac0bfa7206a6386e9ab4f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[49]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0049", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dear Mr. Copperfield,’ said Mrs. Micawber, ‘I wish Mr. Micawber to feel his position. It appears to me highly important that Mr. Micawber should, from the hour of his embarkation, feel his position. Your old knowledge of me, my dear Mr. Copperfield, will have told you that I have not the sanguine disposition of Mr. Micawber. My disposition is, if I may say so, eminently practical. I know that this is a long voyage. I know that it will involve many privations and inconveniences. I cannot shut my eyes to those facts. But I also know what Mr. Micawber is. I know the latent power of Mr. Micawber. And therefore I consider it vitally important that Mr. Micawber should feel his position.’", "sha256": "074ae008734720e3a8776cf8fc5d3dfa35b79b9344cdc3c845c88038d53b69b2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[50]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0050", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My love,’ he observed, ‘perhaps you will allow me to remark that it is barely possible that I DO feel my position at the present moment.’", "sha256": "5067a8da55e065b87f73d047a870c80ebd26e09afb8bf5a7a61a24c2716a7108", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[51]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0051", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I think not, Micawber,’ she rejoined. ‘Not fully. My dear Mr. Copperfield, Mr. Micawber’s is not a common case. Mr. Micawber is going to a distant country expressly in order that he may be fully understood and appreciated for the first time. I wish Mr. Micawber to take his stand upon that vessel’s prow, and firmly say, “This country I am come to conquer! Have you honours? Have you riches? Have you posts of profitable pecuniary emolument? Let them be brought forward. They are mine!”’", "sha256": "f4a59e6f79d42f9de991eb616710178706552334879a59c2ff51bd61e59debbe", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[52]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0052", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber, glancing at us all, seemed to think there was a good deal in this idea.", "sha256": "bd70fcca8329d85041c064077c5626ba50bbfd25b5bd7542d693533bfb61d69f", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[53]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0053", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I wish Mr. Micawber, if I make myself understood,’ said Mrs. Micawber, in her argumentative tone, ‘to be the Caesar of his own fortunes. That, my dear Mr. Copperfield, appears to me to be his true position. From the first moment of this voyage, I wish Mr. Micawber to stand upon that vessel’s prow and say, “Enough of delay: enough of disappointment: enough of limited means. That was in the old country. This is the new. Produce your reparation. Bring it forward!”’", "sha256": "0fe722e1fb0cef76f58348b1ae19d4aba60cf1890567f2160a3e1ef4d89f7212", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[54]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0054", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber folded his arms in a resolute manner, as if he were then stationed on the figure-head.", "sha256": "dc5026b7b0042e0f3e65f15d068f190cac95247caa350301bd2d4ba7643c7505", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[55]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0055", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And doing that,’ said Mrs. Micawber, ‘—feeling his position—am I not right in saying that Mr. Micawber will strengthen, and not weaken, his connexion with Britain? An important public character arising in that hemisphere, shall I be told that its influence will not be felt at home? Can I be so weak as to imagine that Mr. Micawber, wielding the rod of talent and of power in Australia, will be nothing in England? I am but a woman; but I should be unworthy of myself and of my papa, if I were guilty of such absurd weakness.’", "sha256": "244650787a1a58fb61ab91162dbabffb0c62ce3c2951d120b36af55edf2b7deb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[56]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0056", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mrs. Micawber’s conviction that her arguments were unanswerable, gave a moral elevation to her tone which I think I had never heard in it before.", "sha256": "87825d111cbc4e07e37e10ed9218ff2fe6586fad551de539cd4109f0a6b1d8f6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[57]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0057", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘And therefore it is,’ said Mrs. Micawber, ‘that I the more wish, that, at a future period, we may live again on the parent soil. Mr. Micawber may be—I cannot disguise from myself that the probability is, Mr. Micawber will be—a page of History; and he ought then to be represented in the country which gave him birth, and did NOT give him employment!’", "sha256": "469bc45e953e957758e43be720198134ea06944ce09258b06144dbee603f02bb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[58]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0058", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My love,’ observed Mr. Micawber, ‘it is impossible for me not to be touched by your affection. I am always willing to defer to your good sense. What will be—will be. Heaven forbid that I should grudge my native country any portion of the wealth that may be accumulated by our descendants!’", "sha256": "9a59837ceadd5f48bebb73a37dfbd1e8f6cb1795147c15ed660dbdd56ef23a58", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[59]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0059", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘That’s well,’ said my aunt, nodding towards Mr. Peggotty, ‘and I drink my love to you all, and every blessing and success attend you!’", "sha256": "48162858833b50a6543a03581f4ac0a04974b014c59ce20a0d763b84adc9c8b8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[60]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0060", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Peggotty put down the two children he had been nursing, one on each knee, to join Mr. and Mrs. Micawber in drinking to all of us in return; and when he and the Micawbers cordially shook hands as comrades, and his brown face brightened with a smile, I felt that he would make his way, establish a good name, and be beloved, go where he would.", "sha256": "4b514b64247310d1f717cb0dd2a36f7dac465f55d4afd6400fb3712ab1d6ec13", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[61]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0061", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Even the children were instructed, each to dip a wooden spoon into Mr. Micawber’s pot, and pledge us in its contents. When this was done, my aunt and Agnes rose, and parted from the emigrants. It was a sorrowful farewell. They were all crying; the children hung about Agnes to the last; and we left poor Mrs. Micawber in a very distressed condition, sobbing and weeping by a dim candle, that must have made the room look, from the river, like a miserable light-house.", "sha256": "4daf7b25f89848a86863148df4792795ed0d144e3e57d7a4d40445acb7b7ec89", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[62]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0062", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I went down again next morning to see that they were away. They had departed, in a boat, as early as five o’clock. It was a wonderful instance to me of the gap such partings make, that although my association of them with the tumble-down public-house and the wooden stairs dated only from last night, both seemed dreary and deserted, now that they were gone.", "sha256": "5dd94a2149fc9564f0123ef534c7ee5c2735662ebc0f9d769f8260da3bcdd35c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[63]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u059-b0063", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "In the afternoon of the next day, my old nurse and I went down to Gravesend. We found the ship in the river, surrounded by a crowd of boats; a favourable wind blowing; the signal for sailing at her mast-head. I hired a boat directly, and we put off to her; and getting through the little vortex of confusion of which she was the centre, went on board.", "sha256": "ae6a29711b6f65f8a351a0234627ffb24853a4500ab8a25f6de6caa4ba26fba5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[64]/p[64]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
